Comments: Mozambique lacks a general mandatory data breach notification requirement; DLA Piper notes “There is currently no breach notification requirement in Mozambique.”

Definition: Whether national data protection or privacy legislation exists and explicitly covers payment transaction data, including provisions on data collection, storage, sharing, retention, and user rights over their payment data.
Comments: Mozambique does not appear to have a comprehensive, enacted general data protection law; DLA Piper’s jurisdiction overview notes no specific data protection/privacy law, with sectoral rules (e.g., Electronic Transactions Law, financial sector law) providing privacy obligations.

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing an instant/real-time payment system (IPS/RTP) that enables digital payments with near-instant settlement (typically within seconds), available 24/7/365. This includes both bank-led and mobile money interoperability systems.
Comments: Mozambique has an interoperable instant payment infrastructure (SIMO/SIMOrede) and has also formally established the Mozambique Instant Payment System (SPIM) as a 24/7 retail instant payments mechanism under Notice No. 1/GBM/2026.

Definition: Percentage of government payments (G2P disbursements including salaries, pensions, social transfers) made through instant digital payment system rather than cash or check, reflecting government adoption and modernization.
Comments: Evidence of government payment digitization exists (integration of SIMO with e-SISTAFE enabling P2G; and INAS safety net agency uses e-wallets/prepaid cards/smartcards) but no quantified share of government payments digitized was located; scored as limited/partial adoption.
